_readme.purpose: Language-neutral table for the signup allowlist requirement: whether a custom domain's signup config has at least one domain to admit. The server enforces the rule on save; the workspace form mirrors it to gate Save. Both read this file, so a rule changed on one side fails a test instead of letting the form offer a save the API refuses, or the reverse.

implementations.entrypoint: Onetime::CustomDomain::SignupConfig.allowlist_requirement_error (met when it returns nil; called with corrupt: false)

_readme.scope: Readable lists only. An unreadable stored list is a server-only case (the wire format cannot carry one) and stays in try/unit/models/custom_domain/signup_config_try.rb.

how_to_read_a_case.id: stable, unique slug; both suites put it in the test name
how_to_read_a_case.domains: the listed domains; null means the list is absent
how_to_read_a_case.allow_base_domain: allow_base_domain as it counts: stored true AND available (install flag on, organization entitled). Availability is decided before the rule runs, by SignupConfig.base_domain_signup_available_for? on the server and by the form's props in the browser.
how_to_read_a_case.base_domain: the custom domain's registrable domain, or null when it has none
how_to_read_a_case.met: the answer BOTH implementations must give
how_to_read_a_case.note: optional; present whenever the answer is not obvious

cases.note: The base domain is the whole list.
The flag has nothing to add, so the effective list is empty and the sign-up gate would deny everyone.
Also the case for a stored true that is not available: callers pass false.
